usefulness.example: A company runs 500 candidate submissions for an 'add two integers safely' task. The agent ranks them by correctness, edge-case handling and memory safety, and gives an explainable per-metric score.
usefulness.benefit: Fast first-round filtering where every rejection can be justified metric by metric.

usefulness.use_case: Plagiarism and LLM-copy triage for instructors
usefulness.example: Two submissions reach a similarity of 0.93 against the 0.85 threshold, so the agent raises a flag in the report. The instructor reviews only those pairs instead of all 300.
usefulness.benefit: Saves review time by narrowing manual checking to suspicious cases.

usefulness.use_case: Continuous feedback in large-enrollment university CS labs
usefulness.example: 400 students submitting weekly lab assignments get instant, reproducible feedback at 2 AM without waiting days for TA grading.
usefulness.benefit: Accelerates student learning cycle and unburdens teaching assistants.

usefulness.use_case: CI/CD regression gating for mission-critical C software
usefulness.example: Pull requests must achieve 100/100 across correctness, sanitizers, and complexity bounds before merging into embedded systems firmware.
usefulness.benefit: Intercepts memory leaks and algorithmic latency regressions before production deployment.

limitations.example: A submission passes all 10 hidden tests but fails when the input has extra whitespace or a trailing newline that no test covers. The agent still reports 10/10.
limitations.mitigation: The agent should create its own extra tricky test inputs and compare the student's answers with the answers of a correct program.

limitations.limitation: Wall-clock timing curves are noisy on shared or virtualized machines
limitations.example: A student's O(1) submission runs in 2ms on one execution, but during background OS scheduling spikes to 28ms, distorting empirical complexity estimation.
limitations.mitigation: Normalize timings against a simultaneous baseline kernel or measure hardware instruction counts / CPU cycles instead of raw wall-clock time.

limitations.limitation: Surface similarity can be deceived by structural refactoring and obfuscation
limitations.example: A student copies code from a peer but reorders independent statements, inserts dead variables, or wraps expressions in macros, dropping lexical n-gram similarity below 0.85.
limitations.mitigation: Synthesize control-flow graphs (CFG) and compare normalized intermediate representations (LLVM IR / AST) rather than token text.

limitations.limitation: Compiler optimizations may mask undefined behavior or dead loops
limitations.example: An uninitialized variable or dead infinite loop is eliminated by GCC at -O2 optimization level, allowing a flawed submission to pass smoke tests.
limitations.mitigation: Compile and test across multiple optimization tiers (-O0, -O2, -Og) with ASan/UBSan instrumentation.
